superseded_calls.notes: English paragraph 2 states 'freedom is not formally in the will alone and in the intellect only as cause and root.' but Latin says 'libertatem non esse formaliter, ut multis placet, in sola voluntate; in intellectu vero tantum causaliter & radicaliter', i.e., freedom is not formal in the will alone (as many think), but only causal and radical in the intellect. The English reverses the logic by saying 'not formally in the will alone and in the intellect only as cause and root,' implying freedom is not formal in the will AND not only causal/radical in the intellect, which contradicts the Latin that affirms it is causal/radical in the intellect.
The English translation accurately renders the Latin source paragraph across its three divided English paragraphs without omitting content or altering agency.
